stimulus: A vertical flagpole $BT$ stands on level ground at a visitor site. Points $X$, $Y$ and $B$ lie on the same straight path, with $Y$ between $X$ and $B$ and $XY=20\text{ m}$. The angle of elevation of $T$ from $X$ is $30^\circ$ and the angle of elevation of $T$ from $Y$ is $45^\circ$. Let $YB=d\text{ m}$ and let $BT=h\text{ m}$.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Determine the value of $d$ in exact form.

parts.label: d

slots.label: iii
accept: the two perpendicular sides $YB$ and $BT$ are equal
it has equal legs and a right angle

parts.statement: The height of the flagpole is {} m, correct to 3 significant figures. Triangle $YBT$ is {} because {}.

rubric.criterion: Recognises that $BT$ is perpendicular to the level ground.
rubric.template: Recognises that $BT$ is perpendicular to the level ground.
rubric.hint: Recognise that $BT$ is perpendicular to the level ground, so you can use a right-angled triangle.

rubric.criterion: Selects the tangent ratio for the $45^\circ$ angle of elevation.
rubric.template: Selects the tangent ratio for the $45^\circ$ angle of elevation.
rubric.hint: Select the tangent ratio using the $45^\circ$ angle of elevation.
Simplify $\tan45^\circ=h/d$ to show the relationship between $h$ and $d$.
State the full horizontal distance as $XB=d+20$.
Form $\tan(\text{your angle from (a)})=(d+20)/h$ using your angle from part (a).

rubric.criterion: Substitutes $h=d$ and solves using their angle.
rubric.template: Substitutes $h=d$ and solves using their angle.
rubric.hint: Substitute $h=d$ into your tangent equation and solve for $d$ using your angle from part (a).

rubric.criterion: Uses $h=d$ and their value of $d$ to obtain $h\approx27.3205$.
rubric.template: Uses $h=d$ and their value of $d$ to obtain $h\approx27.3205$.
rubric.hint: Use $h=d$ and your value of $d$ to calculate the unrounded height, writing it as $h\approx\text{(your decimal)}$.

rubric.criterion: Expresses their height correct to 3 significant figures.
rubric.template: Expresses their height correct to 3 significant figures.
rubric.hint: Round your height to 3 significant figures.

rubric.criterion: Identifies triangle $YBT$ as an isosceles right triangle.
rubric.template: Identifies triangle $YBT$ as an isosceles right triangle.
rubric.hint: Identify triangle $YBT$ as an isosceles right triangle.

rubric.criterion: Justifies the classification using equal perpendicular sides.
rubric.template: Justifies the classification using equal perpendicular sides.
rubric.hint: Justify this by showing that $YB=BT$ and that these equal sides meet at a right angle.

worked_solution:
(a) Since the flagpole is vertical and the ground is level, $\angle XBT=90^\circ$. The angle at $X$ is $30^\circ$, so $\angle BTX=90^\circ-30^\circ=60^\circ$.

(b) From $Y$, $\tan45^\circ=\frac{h}{d}$. Since $\tan45^\circ=1$, it follows that $h=d$.

(c) The distance $XB=d+20$. In right triangle $XBT$, using the angle found in (a),
\[
\tan60^\circ=\frac{d+20}{h}.
\]
Using $h=d$ gives $\sqrt{3}=\frac{d+20}{d}$. Therefore $d(\sqrt{3}-1)=20$, so
\[
d=\frac{20}{\sqrt{3}-1}=10(\sqrt{3}+1).
\]

(d) Since $h=d$, the flagpole height is $10(\sqrt{3}+1)\approx27.3205\text{ m}$, giving $27.3\text{ m}$ correct to 3 significant figures. Also, $YB=BT$ and $\angle YBT=90^\circ$, so triangle $YBT$ is an isosceles right triangle.

misconceptions.name: Ignoring the 20 m separation
misconceptions.remediation: The distance from $X$ to the base is not $d$; it is $d+20$. Include the full distance $XB$ when forming the trigonometric ratio.

misconceptions.name: Using the tangent ratio upside down
misconceptions.remediation: For $\angle BTX$, the side opposite is $XB=d+20$ and the adjacent side is $BT=h$. Therefore $\tan60^\circ=(d+20)/h$.

misconceptions.name: Incomplete classification
misconceptions.remediation: Triangle $YBT$ has a right angle and also has equal perpendicular sides, since $YB=BT$. Its full classification is an isosceles right triangle.
